commits.message:
sandbox: Add support for riscv64-linux

Teach the Linux sandbox about riscv64: syscall ranges, seccomp macros
for register and instruction-pointer access, the signal, stat and seccomp
system headers, a new riscv64_linux_syscalls.h, the raw syscall and trap
entry paths, and the riscv64 syscall sets used by the baseline policy and
by every bpf_*_policy_linux.cc.

Without this, riscv64 does not build at all: seccomp_macros.h ends its
architecture chain with '#error Unsupported target platform', and
linux_syscalls.h has no riscv64 include. It is not optional at runtime
either -- the WebView renderer runs with SECCOMP_MODE_FILTER, so the
policy has to know the riscv64 syscall numbering.

Origin: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/4935120
patchset 11, not merged upstream.

Two files from that changelist are deliberately not carried here, both
test-only: syscall_parameters_restrictions_unittest.cc no longer exists
upstream, and the riscv branch for syscall_unittest.cc (an ECALL opcode
assertion) is missing. Neither is built by the WebView target.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume La Roque <glaroque@baylibre.com>

build/config: riscv64: build with -mstrict-align

The SpacemiT X60 traps on misaligned vector accesses, and the kernel
misaligned handler emulates only unit-stride vle/vse, not the strided
vlse the autovectorizer emits. WebView died with SIGBUS/BUS_ADRALN on
the first loadUrl before this. The rationale is kept next to the flag.

Note that this applies to every riscv64 build, not only SpacemiT parts;
hardware with working misaligned vector support pays for alignment it
does not need.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume La Roque <glaroque@baylibre.com>

android: do not apply the 32-bit version code offset on riscv64

The offset exists for 64-bit targets that ship a paired 32-bit secondary
ABI. riscv64 has no secondary ABI, so applying it produces a version code
from the wrong range.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume La Roque <glaroque@baylibre.com>

cpuinfo: enable the riscv linux sources on android

riscv/linux/init.c and riscv-hw.c were gated on is_linux || is_chromeos,
so an android riscv64 build compiled no cpuinfo backend at all. Android
uses the same Linux hwprobe and /proc interfaces. Upstreamable as is.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume La Roque <glaroque@baylibre.com>

ffmpeg: support the android-riscv64 build

Add riscv64 to the android entry of ARCH_MAP and teach
SetupAndroidToolchain about it. API 35 is the first NDK level with a
riscv64 sysroot, so the toolchain level is pinned there rather than
following api64_level.

The companion changes live in the third_party/ffmpeg repository and are
therefore not part of this commit: ffmpeg_generated.gni, and the
generated configuration under
chromium/config/Chrome/android/riscv64/ (10 files). That directory must
be present for the build to succeed -- this script only makes generating
it possible.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume La Roque <glaroque@baylibre.com>

blink: fix SimdEqualIgnoringAsciiCase tag types for scalable vectors

SimdEqualIgnoringAsciiCase() builds its 8-bit descriptor as an independent
FixedTag<uint8_t, 8> and promotes it to FixedTag<uint16_t, 8>. On fixed-width
targets the two descriptors agree, but on a scalable-vector target such as
RVV, PromoteTo expects VFromD<Rebind<uint8_t, D>>, whose LMUL is half of
FixedTag<uint8_t, 8>'s, so overload resolution fails:

  string_impl.h:815: error: no matching function for call to 'PromoteTo'

Rebind is what the Highway API intends here and is correct on every target.
Upstreamable as is -- this code has simply never been compiled for RVV, since
upstream does not build Chromium for android riscv64.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume La Roque <glaroque@baylibre.com>

skia: link the NDK ICU stub when building against API 31 or newer

SkFontMgr_android_ndk.cpp reaches u_strFoldCase, u_strFromUTF8 and
u_strToUTF8 two different ways: it dlsym's them out of libicu.so below API
31, and references them directly from API 31 on. Nothing links the NDK ICU
stub, so the direct path leaves three undefined symbols in
libwebviewchromium.so:

  ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: u_strFoldCase
  >>> referenced by SkFontMgr_android_ndk.cpp:178

Only riscv64 reaches that path today. build/config/android/config.gni pins
android_ndk_api_level to 36 for riscv64 -- 'Android did not support RISC-V64
before API 36' -- while every other architecture compiles against Chromium's
much lower min sdk and therefore always takes the dlsym path.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume La Roque <glaroque@baylibre.com>
